# Comparison with Claude Code

Dimension 6 of 7 for [Goose AI Agent](../citations.md) research.

## Benchmark Performance

| Benchmark | Claude Code | Goose | Gap |
|-----------|------------|-------|-----|
| SWE-bench Verified (Sonnet 4.5) | 72.7% | ~45% | 27+ points [26] |
| SWE-bench Verified (Opus 4.5) | 80.9% | N/A | — [26] |
| Terminal-Bench | 3rd | 4th | 1 rank [30] |
| Avg task completion | 10 min (est.) | 12 min | 2 min [29] |

The 27-point SWE-bench gap with the same underlying model (Sonnet 4.5) indicates that Claude Code's "agent orchestration, tool use patterns, and Anthropic's fine-tuning of the agentic loop" add significant capability beyond the model itself [26].

An independent observation: "scaffolding matters as much as the model" — three frameworks running identical models scored 17 issues apart on 731 problems [26].

## Architecture Differences

### Goose

- ReAct loop foundation [1]
- Extensions = MCP servers [6]
- Recipes for workflow automation (YAML) [10]
- Per-session context isolation [37]
- Model-agnostic — swap with `goose configure` [3]
- Dual protocol (MCP for tools, ACP for clients) [1]

### Claude Code

- Dedicated agentic execution layer with model-specific optimizations
- Skills: reusable workflow macros with YAML frontmatter, auto-invocation
- Hooks: 15+ lifecycle events with deterministic command/HTTP/prompt handlers
- Agent Teams: 2-16 coordinated sessions with shared task list, peer messaging, file locking
- Agent SDK for custom pipelines
- CLAUDE.md project memory hierarchy (enterprise/user/project/directory levels)
- 1M context window with extended thinking
- Prompt caching built into the platform

## Extension and Automation Comparison

### Goose Recipes vs Claude Code Hooks + Skills

**Recipes** are YAML workflow packages with parameter interpolation, sub-recipe composition, cron scheduling, and extension pinning [10]. They are shareable — designed for team standardization [28].

**Claude Code Skills** are markdown-defined reusable workflows with YAML frontmatter, auto-invocation triggers, and argument substitution. **Hooks** provide deterministic automation on 15 lifecycle events — unlike LLM-driven decisions, hooks execute 100% of the time when triggered [26].

Key difference: Goose recipes are LLM-interpreted YAML (probabilistic execution) [10]. Claude Code hooks are deterministic shell/HTTP commands triggered by events (guaranteed execution).

### Multi-Agent

**Goose subagents:** Max 10 concurrent (hard-coded), 5-min timeout, 25 max turns, no nesting, experimental [37]. External subagents can use other providers via MCP [41].

**Claude Code Agent Teams:** 2-16 coordinated sessions with bidirectional messaging, shared task lists with dependency tracking, file locking, 3-7x token consumption [26].

## Privacy and Data Control

**Goose:** All prompts, code, and outputs can remain on the local machine. Zero cloud dependency with Ollama or Docker Model Runner [3]. With cloud models, data goes to the selected provider's API.

**Claude Code:** Code is processed on Anthropic's cloud servers. Anthropic states it doesn't train on API inputs by default, but code does leave the local machine [26].

With cloud models, Goose's cost advantage over Claude Code is "modest to nonexistent" ($5-20/month vs $20/month) [27]. The $0 local option requires ~$4,000+ hardware (est.) [27].

## Counter-Perspectives

### Claude Code Weaknesses

- **Vendor lock-in:** Single-model dependency on Anthropic [26]
- **No local/offline option:** Code always leaves the machine [26]
- **No BYOM:** Cannot use non-Claude models [26]
- **Usage limits:** March 2026 crisis — sessions draining in 1-2 hours instead of 5 [32]

### Goose Weaknesses

- **Benchmark gap:** 27-point SWE-bench deficit with same model [26]
- **Setup complexity:** 7.50/10 vs Cursor's 2.00/10 [29]
- **Model-dependent quality:** Output varies dramatically based on model choice [29]
- **Not zero-config:** Requires terminal comfort, YAML editing, log reading [29]
- **Recipe regression:** v1.25.0 systematically deviates from recipe instructions [49]

### Scoring Discrepancy

One source (Effloow) scored Goose AgentScore 7.7/10 vs Claude Code 5.3/10 [25]. This inverted ranking relative to SWE-bench reflects different evaluation criteria — Effloow weights cost, flexibility, and extensibility heavily, while SWE-bench measures raw code generation capability.

## Decision Framework

Choose Goose if: zero-budget baseline, multi-provider flexibility, on-machine privacy, open-source auditability, JetBrains native integration, shareable team recipes [26].

Choose Claude Code if: peak benchmark performance, coordinated multi-agent (Agent Teams), deterministic automation (hooks), predictable flat cost, production-grade quality [26].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No head-to-head benchmark with same model, same task, controlled conditions
- SWE-bench gap source (Morph LLM) methodology not fully described
- Claude Code pricing may have changed since sources were published
- No comparison of real-world developer productivity (only synthetic benchmarks)
